text:
Data Science with AI · UC San Diego · June 2026
Question. After Coca-Cola Zero’s 2017 and 2021 reformulations, what were consumers actually complaining about — and did complaint volume change?
Approach. Pulled a 57,000-post consumer corpus and classified every post into 16 complaint categories with an R and LLM API pipeline, using JSON-schema enforced outputs, retry logic, and corpus trimming to control cost. Hand-coding the same corpus at one minute per post would have taken roughly 950 analyst-hours.
Finding. Event-study difference-in-differences showed how complaint volume shifted around each reformulation, and which categories drove the change.
Recommendation. Delivered as a one-page memo written for brand leadership rather than for analysts.

section: Ergonomic Pen Concept — End-to-End Market Research
text:
Ergonomic Pen Concept — End-to-End Market Research
Applied Market Research · UC San Diego · 2025 · Conducted for an early-stage consumer product concept
Question. Is there demand for an ergonomic pen concept, who would buy it, and what would they pay?
Approach. Fielded a 500+ respondent Qualtrics survey measuring feature preference and willingness to pay inside a $17.5B global writing-instrument market, benchmarked against BIC, Pilot, and Paper Mate.
Finding. Segmented respondents across demographic, psychographic, and occupational dimensions to identify which groups carried real willingness to pay.
Recommendation. Delivered a SWOT, a segmentation map, and the positioning statement “Precision Meets Comfort.”

section: Causal Evaluation of a Crisis-Response Program — Denver STAR
text:
Causal Evaluation of a Crisis-Response Program — Denver STAR
Business Analytics · UC San Diego · April 2026 · Team of 3
Question. Does dispatching mental-health clinicians instead of police actually reduce low-level offenses?
Approach. Difference-in-differences across 386,865 incident records, 78 neighborhoods, and 44 months — separating 8 treated neighborhoods from 70 controls and modeling COVID-19 time trends explicitly so the pandemic shock couldn’t be misread as program effect.
Finding. Peer-reviewed across UC San Diego Rady and Northwestern Kellogg sections.

section: Pay Equity Analysis — NFL Salaries vs. Regional Cost of Living
text:
Pay Equity Analysis — NFL Salaries vs. Regional Cost of Living
Business Analytics · UC San Diego · March 2026 · Team of 5
Question. Do teams in expensive cities pay quarterbacks more?
Approach. Merged NFL contract data with U.S. regional cost-of-living indices, then re-ran every model with and without outlier treatment.
Finding. No meaningful correlation — a null result.
Recommendation. Advised against cost-of-living adjustments in cap strategy rather than overstating a weak correlation.

title: About
text:
I’m a UC San Diego Business Psychology graduate focused on consumer insights and market research. My work pairs behavioral frameworks and survey methodology with applied analytics, turning what consumers say and do into a recommendation a team can act on.
While earning my degree I was also the primary caregiver for my family, so instead of internships I took freelance research and data work alongside a full course load.
